newsitem.title: BERMUDA: Bermuda licenses 97 new insurers in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Bermuda licenses 97 new insurers in 1996.

text.p: The Bermuda government said it licensed 97 new insurance companies in 1996, up from 90 in 1995, and said 28 insurers were removed from its register in 1996, down from 46 in 1995.

The additions brought the total number of registered international insurers in Bermuda to 1,470 and made last year the highest for incorporation activity since 1986 when 125 new insurers were created, according to statistics released late Thursday by the Bermuda Registrar of Companies.
Thirty of the new insurers licensed in 1996, or about one-third, were Class 3 companies, the government said.

Class 3 companies are defined under Bermuda's system as including finite reinsurers, insurers writing direct policies with third-party individuals and captives deriving more than 20 percent of net premiums from unrelated risks.
More than half of the new licenses, or a total of 51, were issued to Class 1 or Class 2 companies.
Class 1 and Class 2 companies are captive insurers, which insure the risks of their owners or affiliates of the owners.
Only three, or about three percent, of the licenses were issued to Class 4 companies, insurers and reinsurers underwriting direct excess liability and/or property catastrophe reinsurance risk.

The origin of Bermuda's 1996 insurance corporations, as measured by the domiciles of the beneficial owners, was broadly similar to that of 1995, with the majority of the new insurers coming from the United States and Europe, the government said.
However, the domiciles of the beneficial owners also included non-traditional markets such as Australia, Canada, Central and South America and the Far East.
